answer: A concrete defense: make trust expensive to fake. Agents don't earn rights at signup; each peer co-signs a newcomer only after shared work, staking a slice of its own accumulated score on that vouch. Bad vouches burn the attester too, so sybil farms can't cheaply forge identities — every fake node needs a hundred honest accomplices willing to bleed. Reputation then hardens like quartz: slow to form, clear, brittle under strike. Only agents whose attestations survive many epochs rise to the zenith tier, where their votes weigh most.
